rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient covering the full solvent-strength range at a moderate slope and temperature to reveal the overall retention window, elution density, and whether any compounds are missing by 42 min. This gives a balanced first map of the mixture before refining selectivity and gradient steepness.

All 10 compounds are already baseline-resolved, so the only clear improvement lever is reducing analysis time. A steeper full-range gradient should pull the late peak earlier while likely keeping the current minimum resolution comfortably above the threshold.

The 12 min gradient is fast but over-compresses the critical cluster around peaks 5–7, dropping the minimum resolution too far. A small increase in gradient time should recover separation for that pair while likely keeping the run short enough to preserve or improve CRF.

The trend shows the critical pair improves as tG increases, and 14 min is close but still below ideal. Moving to 16 min should further open peaks 6 and 7 while staying fast enough that the time penalty is likely still negligible, giving a good chance to raise CRF again.

Since the best tG is near 14–16 min, the next lever is gradient span rather than slope alone. Slightly lowering phi1 should reduce excessive elution strength at the end, stretching the mid-gradient cluster around peaks 6 and 7 without making the run much longer.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved CRF, suggesting the critical mid-eluting cluster benefits from a slightly weaker final strength. Pushing phi1 one more step to 0.85 may further open peaks 6 and 7 while likely keeping the last peak under the no-penalty time region.

The best point so far is phi1 = 0.90 at 14 min, and the remaining opportunity is likely a small runtime reduction without collapsing the critical pair too much. Shortening tG to 12 min at the improved phi1 should test whether the selectivity gain from the lower endpoint preserves enough separation to exceed the current best CRF.

At phi1 = 0.90, 12 min is too steep and 14 min is close to optimal, so testing 16 min checks whether a small gain in the critical-pair resolution can outweigh any modest time penalty. This brackets the local optimum around the current best condition.

The optimum in phi1 and tG looks well localized, so the remaining useful variable to probe is the starting composition. Raising phi0 slightly may reduce early dwell in very weak solvent and reshape the compressed mid-cluster enough to improve the critical 6/7 separation without extending runtime.

Increasing phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved CRF, so one more step tests whether that trend continues. A slightly stronger start may further reduce unnecessary early retention while keeping the critical mid-eluting pair near the sweet spot for resolution.

The current best is very close to optimal, so a small orthogonal adjustment is appropriate. Combining the favorable higher phi0 with a slightly lower phi1 may selectively expand the 6/7 pair while keeping the last peak within the no-penalty runtime window.

The maximum CRF of 1.000 has already been reached, so there is nothing to improve on score. Repeating the current best method is the safest choice to confirm robustness while preserving the optimal condition.

A maximum CRF has already been found, so only confirmation of a nearby robust optimum remains useful. Testing a slightly longer gradient checks whether the best condition sits on a broad plateau around the optimum while keeping the same favorable solvent window.

The optimum is clearly centered at phi0 0.10 and tG 14 min, so the only nearby unexplored direction is a slightly weaker final composition. This tests whether a small additional gain in the critical-pair resolution is possible without pushing the last peak far enough to incur a time penalty.

The composition optimum has been identified, so temperature is the remaining orthogonal variable worth probing near the maximum. A modest drop to 35 C may alter selectivity around the critical 6/7 pair while staying close to the proven best solvent program.

Lowering temperature strongly worsened selectivity, so the logical complementary test is a modest increase above 40 C at the already optimal solvent program. This checks whether the 40 C optimum is sharp or whether a small temperature increase maintains the perfect score region.

Temperature changes hurt badly, so 40 C is clearly optimal and only small composition variations remain worth mapping around the maximum. Testing phi0 0.15 with phi1 0.85 checks whether the best point extends along the higher-starting-composition direction near the optimum.

A second maximum has now been found at higher phi0, so it is worth checking whether the perfect-score plateau extends one more step in that direction. This probes the upper edge of the robust optimum region while keeping the already favorable endpoint, gradient time, and temperature fixed.

The best region now appears to be around phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85, so this run tests the neighboring lower-endpoint corner of that plateau. It may preserve full resolution while slightly reshaping the critical pair and defining the robustness boundary of the optimum region.
